# SchedJoules Calendar Service API

> REST API (JSON over HTTPS) for public calendars: holidays, sports, TV, weather, finance and more. Clients browse pages of calendars and subscribe users to calendar feed URLs (iCalendar); JSCalendar (RFC 8984), the recommended format for new integrations, gives a calendar as a slim list and a single event as a document for detail screens. jCal and xCal still work but are not recommended. Every request needs an `Authorization: Token token="..."` header.

Generated from the markdown files in this repository by .github/scripts/build_llms.py. Do not edit by hand.


<!-- source: README.md -->

## SchedJoules Calendar Service API

This API provides access to the SchedJoules Public Calendar Service: public calendars for holidays, sports, TV, weather, financial events and more, for desktop, web and mobile applications, in 18 languages.

**New here? Start with the [Integration Guide](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/integration_guide.md).** Reading this with a coding agent? Give it [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/AGENTS.md) and [llms-full.txt](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/llms-full.txt), which holds every page in one file. Example responses and feeds are in [examples/](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/tree/master/examples).

## SDKs

The iOS and Android SDKs and the Swift client library are deprecated: integrate the REST API directly. See [SDKs](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/sdks.md).

## Set Yourself Up

An API key is required. Request one at support@schedjoules.com.

You can explore the API with our test API key:
```
curl 'https://api.schedjoules.com/pages/115673' -H 'Authorization: Token token="0443a55244bb2b6224fd48e0416f0d9c"'
```
The test key gives access to the complete API, and every calendar URL it returns serves that calendar's real events, limited to the next 5. Your own key returns the whole calendar, in the window your agreement gives.

## Request Basics

| | |
|---|---|
| Base URL | `https://api.schedjoules.com/` |
| Authentication | Header `Authorization: Token token="{YOUR_API_KEY}"` |
| Format | JSON. Appending `.json` to a URL is not required |
| Transport | HTTPS. A plain HTTP request is redirected to HTTPS |
| Redirects | `GET /pages` answers with a `302` to the page it resolves to. Follow redirects |

A missing or unknown API key returns `401`:
```json
{"errors": {"status": 401, "title": "Invalid API key", "detail": "https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api#set-yourself-up"}}
```

### Versioning
There is one version, `v1`. You may send `Accept: application/vnd.schedjoules; version=1`, but it is optional and currently every request is served by v1.

Fields may be added to responses without a version change, so make sure your client ignores fields it does not know.

### Language
The response language is taken from, in this order:
1. the `locale` parameter
2. the `x-locale` header
3. the `Accept-Language` header

Only the first two letters are used, so `de_DE` and `de-AT` both mean `de`. `nb` is read as `no`. A language the API does not support falls back to English. See [Languages](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/languages.md) for the list.

## Pages
The API is built around pages. A page represents a view in your application: for example, a football page lists all teams in a league, so the user can pick a team and add its matches to their calendar.

Start from the user's location:
```
GET /pages?locale={ISO 639-1 code}&location={ISO 3166 code}

Optional GET parameters
- locale        language of the response (see Language above)
- location      ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. Without it, or with an unknown one,
                you get the default catalogue of your API key, or the general
                "All Calendars" page
```

Or open a page by its id:
```
GET /pages/{page_id}?locale={ISO 639-1 code}
```

[ISO 639-1 language codes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639-1_codes) · [ISO 3166 country codes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2)

A page has a name and a list of `page_sections`. A section works as a header or grouping within the page, and holds items whose `item_class` is either `page` or `calendar`:
* A `page` item is a child page. For example, "English Football" is a child of "All Football", and "Premier League" is a child of "English Football".
* A `calendar` item is the calendar itself: its `url` is the feed your user subscribes to.

See [Pages](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/pages.md) for the full response format.

## Unique Anonymous User Identifier
Before presenting a calendar URL to your users, append a unique anonymous user identifier to it: `&u={unique_anonymous_user_identifier}`. It is used for statistics and to detect and prevent misuse of our content. Use the same identifier for the same user everywhere, including the [Accounts API](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/accounts.md).

## Caching
Cache responses wherever possible.
* API responses carry an `ETag` and a `Last-Modified` header, and answer `304 Not Modified` to a matching `If-None-Match` or `If-Modified-Since`.
* They are sent with `Cache-Control: max-age=0, private, must-revalidate`: keep your copy, but revalidate it before using it again.

## Rate Limits
There are currently no rate limits. Requests are monitored, and we may reach out if we see a way to make your integration more efficient.

## Data Usage and Restrictions
By using this API, you acknowledge that all accessed data is proprietary. The data and images may not be used for any purpose beyond what has been agreed upon. Data may not be stored in any database other than on a user's client device for performance purposes.

## Attribution
Every screen where users browse, search or pick SchedJoules calendars shows the line **Calendars by SchedJoules**, unless your agreement with us says otherwise.

* Plain text in your secondary text style is enough; a logo is not required. You may link it to `https://www.schedjoules.com`.
* Translate "Calendars by" with the rest of your app; keep "SchedJoules" as it is.
* It must be visible where the content is chosen: an About screen or a footer elsewhere in the app does not count.
* Where it goes on each screen: [A Basic UI](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/ui.md#attribution) and [Embedding the Catalogue](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/embedding.md#attribution).

## Feedback and Support
If you have a feature request or have found a bug, open a GitHub issue or email support@schedjoules.com.

## Integration Guide

The shortest path from nothing to a calendar app that shows SchedJoules calendars. It ties the reference pages together and adds the rules that only show up once real users sync real feeds. Screens: [A Basic UI](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/ui.md) for a separate catalogue, [Embedding](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/embedding.md) to put it inside an existing app. Platform specifics: [Android](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/android.md) and [iOS](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/ios.md). Example responses and feeds: [examples/](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/tree/master/examples).

### The model in one paragraph

The API is a catalogue: pages of calendars, in the user's language and country. Your app shows the catalogue, the user picks a calendar, and from then on your app fetches that calendar's events regularly. A calendar item has a `url` that serves the events in two formats, and steps 1 to 3 are the same for both:

* **JSCalendar** ([RFC 8984](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8984)), the recommended format: plain JSON with structured data, a slim list of the calendar's events, and the full details of one event when the user opens it.
* **iCalendar** ([RFC 5545](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5545)), the most widely used format, and what the `url` returns as it is.

JSCalendar can be used for subscribing and syncing too, but most calendar clients (the iOS and Android calendars, Google Calendar, Outlook) read only iCalendar. That is why this guide syncs into a device calendar from iCalendar. If you do sync from JSCalendar, the list alone is not enough: it has titles and times but no descriptions, so you also need each event's own document. After step 3 it splits into two tracks, and many apps follow both. See [Which Format to Use](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/calendars.md#which-format-to-use).

### Step 1: a key and the request basics

Use the test key from the [README](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api#set-yourself-up) to build everything; request your own key before you ship. Every API request needs:

```
Authorization: Token token="{YOUR_API_KEY}"
```

Send `locale` (the user's language) and `location` (the user's country) on page requests. Follow redirects. Ignore response fields you do not know.

### Step 2: show the catalogue

1. `GET /pages?locale=de&location=de` gives the home page for that user. It redirects to `/pages/{id}`.
2. Render each section of `page_sections` as a header with its `items`.
3. An item with `item_class: "page"` opens another page: `GET` its `url`.
4. An item with `item_class: "calendar"` is subscribable.

Add search with `GET /pages/search?q=...` (3 characters or more). For the screens around it, see [A Basic UI](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/ui.md). See [Pages](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/pages.md) and [Search](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/search.md).

Store the `item_id` of each calendar the user subscribes to: you need it later (step 5).

### Step 3: build the feed URL

Take the calendar item's `url` as it is, and append the user identifier:

```
{url}&u={unique_anonymous_user_identifier}
```

Rules:
* `u` is a random identifier you create once per user (or install), at least 20 characters. A UUID works. Use the same value for every feed of that user, and as the account id in the [Accounts API](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/accounts.md) if you use it.
* Never remove or change the other parameters, `x` in particular: it identifies your API key on the feed.
* A `url` that contains `{placeholders}` is a template. Fill every placeholder first (the weather calendar's `{location}` and units, see [Weather](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/weather.md)). Never fetch or subscribe to a URL that still contains `{` or `%7B`.
* The feed URL is per user. Do not log it or send it to analytics.

### Step 4: choose a track

| Your app | Track | Format |
|---|---|---|
| Shows events in its own screens: an agenda, upcoming matches, an event page | [A: show events in your app](#track-a-show-events-in-your-app) | JSCalendar |
| Puts events in the device calendar, or in a calendar client that reads iCalendar | [B: sync into a calendar](#track-b-sync-into-a-calendar) | iCalendar |

An app that does both, for example one that syncs into the device calendar and opens an event page of its own, follows both tracks with the same feed URL from step 3.

### Track A: show events in your app

#### Step A1: list a calendar's events

Add `.jscalendar` to the path of the feed URL from step 3 and `GET` it with `Accept: application/jscalendar+json`. Keep every parameter, `u` included. The answer is the whole calendar as a JSCalendar `Group`: each event with its `uid`, `updated`, `title`, `start`, `timeZone` (or `showWithoutTime`), `duration`, `status` and `locations`, a fraction of the iCalendar feed's size. See [A Calendar as a JSCalendar List](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/calendars.md#a-calendar-as-a-jscalendar-list).

* A calendar without events gives `"entries": []`. There are no placeholder events in JSCalendar.
* Access problems are HTTP statuses: `403` with `{"error":"no_access"}` (a bug in your URL, fix it) or `{"error":"expired_subscription"}` (offer renewal).
* Refresh with `If-None-Match` and the last `ETag`, as in step B3: an unchanged list answers `304` with no body.

#### Step A2: show one event

When the user opens an event, fetch it as JSCalendar instead of parsing `DESCRIPTION`: take the same `.jscalendar` URL and append `&event={event part}`, the part of the `uid` after `{item_id}_{language_id}_` (drop `@schedjoules.com`). The document has the same title and time as the list, plus the description, links and structured data such as a match's line-ups, a race classification or a holiday's background. A `404` means the event is no longer in the calendar. On anything other than `200` or `304`, show what you already have. See [One Event as JSCalendar](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/calendars.md#one-event-as-jscalendar-rfc-8984).

### Track B: sync into a calendar

#### Step B1: fetch the feed

`GET` the feed URL. It returns `text/calendar` (iCalendar, [RFC 5545](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5545)). Use it for subscribing and syncing: most calendar clients read only iCalendar, and the rules in this track are written for it. Do not sync from jCal or xCal; they work but are not recommended. When your app also opens events in its own screens, fetch those as JSCalendar (step A2).

What a feed contains:
* `X-WR-CALNAME`: the calendar's name. In your UI you can use the catalogue item's `name` instead (from search results, use `original_name`: search names can end in a gender sign and a flag to tell teams apart).
* One `VEVENT` per event, with `UID`, `DTSTART`, `DTEND`, `SUMMARY`, `DESCRIPTION`, `LOCATION`, `URL`, `LAST-MODIFIED`, `CATEGORIES`, `STATUS`, `TRANSP:TRANSPARENT` and often a `VALARM` (see [Alarms](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/alarms.md)).
* All-day events use `DTSTART;VALUE=DATE` with an exclusive `DTEND`, as the RFC says. Some feeds, the placeholder events among them, send `DTEND` equal to `DTSTART`: treat that as a one-day event.
* `UID` looks like `{item_id}_{language_id}_{rest}@schedjoules.com` and is stable: the same event keeps its UID across fetches. The language is part of it, so the same event in another language has another UID.

**Check the body before you use it.** Only accept a response that starts with `BEGIN:VCALENDAR` and ends with `END:VCALENDAR`. A proxy error page or a cut-off download otherwise looks like a calendar with no events, and your sync deletes everything.

#### Step B2: recognise placeholder events

A feed never answers an access problem with an HTTP error. It answers `200` with one placeholder event that explains the problem to the user. Recognise them by `UID`:

| UID | Meaning | What your app should do |
|---|---|---|
| `no_access@schedjoules.com` | The URL is wrong: missing or invalid `x`, missing `u`, inactive key | A bug on your side. Do not show it as an event; log it and fix the URL |
| `expired_subscription@schedjoules.com` | The user's access ended (for example an expired license in the [Accounts API](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/accounts.md)) | Offer renewal; keep or hide the calendar |
| `expired_{language}@schedjoules.com` | The calendar itself was retired | Remove the subscription, or offer a replacement (step 5) |
| `empty_{item_id}@schedjoules.com` | The calendar has no events in the date range right now | A normal state. Show "no upcoming events" rather than the event |

The placeholder events also carry `CATEGORIES:Expired` or `CATEGORIES:No access`. A placeholder feed also changes `X-WR-CALNAME` (for example to "You have no access to this calendar"): never copy it over the name you show for the calendar. Example feeds: [examples/feeds](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/tree/master/examples/feeds).

#### Step B3: keep it in sync

**Refresh.** Fetch each feed every few hours. Send `If-None-Match` with the last `ETag`: an unchanged feed answers `304 Not Modified` with no body, which costs almost nothing. More often than hourly gains nothing for most calendars; live sport scores change during matches only.

**Apply changes by UID.** Compare the new feed with what you stored:
* a UID you do not have: add the event
* a UID you have: update it if anything changed (`LAST-MODIFIED` helps)
* a UID that is gone from a complete feed: delete the event

**Incremental updates** with `events_updated_since` are optional (see [Calendars](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/calendars.md#incremental-updates)). They never tell you what was deleted, so still fetch the complete feed regularly, for example once a day, and delete only based on complete feeds.

### Both tracks

#### Step 5: replaced calendars

A calendar can be replaced by a newer one, for example a sport season by the next. The old feed URL keeps working and serves the new content, so nothing breaks. To update what you store and show:

```
GET /pages/{item_id}/info
```

returns the calendar's current `item` (name, `url`, icon) and the pages it is listed on, and

```
GET /pages/{calendar_id}/ultimate_successor
```

returns `{"requested_id": "...", "successor_id": "...", "in_api": true}` for the `calendar_id` in a feed URL (`/calendars/{calendar_id}`).

#### Step 6: errors

API errors (not feeds or JSCalendar documents) answer with an HTTP status and:

```json
{"errors": {"status": 401, "title": "Invalid API key", "detail": "https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api#set-yourself-up"}}
```

| Status | Title | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| 401 | Invalid API key | Missing or unknown key |
| 403 | This API key is inactive | The key was switched off; contact us |
| 404 | Nothing here | Unknown page or route |
| 405 | This request is not allowed with this API key | The endpoint is not enabled for your key, for example licenses |
| 500 | Something went wrong | On our side; retry later |

### A v0.1 checklist

- [ ] Every request sends the `Authorization` header; responses are parsed leniently
- [ ] Catalogue browsing with `locale` and `location` from the device, following redirects
- [ ] Feed URL = item `url` + `&u=`, templates filled, nothing else changed
- [ ] Feed URLs never logged

Track A, events in your app:
- [ ] Event lists read the JSCalendar list; an empty calendar shows "no upcoming events"
- [ ] Event detail screens read the event as JSCalendar, falling back to what you have on any non-200
- [ ] `403` answers handled: `no_access` logged as a bug, `expired_subscription` offers renewal

Track B, sync into a calendar:
- [ ] Feed body checked for `BEGIN:VCALENDAR` ... `END:VCALENDAR` before use
- [ ] Placeholder UIDs handled, not shown as events
- [ ] Refresh with `If-None-Match`; changes applied by UID; deletions only from complete feeds


<!-- source: details/android.md -->

## Android

Android has no built-in way to subscribe to an iCalendar feed. Your app fetches the feeds itself and writes the events into the system calendar through `CalendarContract`, so they show up in Google Calendar and every other calendar app on the device. This page lists what that takes, from the SchedJoules Android app's own implementation. Read the [Integration Guide](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/integration_guide.md) first.

### Architecture

* **Fetching:** a `WorkManager` periodic job (with a network constraint) fetches every subscribed feed. Send `If-None-Match` and do nothing more on a `304`.
* **Parsing:** an iCalendar library such as [biweekly](https://github.com/mangstadt/biweekly).
* **Storage:** one local calendar per subscription in `CalendarContract.Calendars`, under your own account type, with events in `CalendarContract.Events`.

You need the `READ_CALENDAR` and `WRITE_CALENDAR` permissions. Ask for them when the user subscribes to their first calendar, after explaining why, not at app start.

### Writing calendars and events

* Write as a sync adapter: append `CALLER_IS_SYNCADAPTER=true`, `ACCOUNT_NAME` and `ACCOUNT_TYPE` (your own, for example your package name) to the content URI. Use `ACCOUNT_TYPE_LOCAL` only if you accept that it behaves differently on some devices.
* One calendar row per subscription. Put your subscription id in `Calendars._SYNC_ID`, and the feed's name in `CALENDAR_DISPLAY_NAME`.
* Put the event `UID` in `Events._SYNC_ID`. On each sync, compare by `_SYNC_ID`: insert new UIDs, update changed ones, delete the ones a complete feed no longer has.
* Apply the changes with `applyBatch`, in chunks of a few hundred operations: one Binder transaction is limited to about 1 MB, and a large sport or TV calendar can exceed it in one go.

### Dates and times

* **All-day events** (`DTSTART;VALUE=DATE`): set `ALL_DAY=1`, `EVENT_TIMEZONE=UTC`, and `DTSTART` at **UTC midnight** of the date. Many parsers, biweekly among them, read a date as midnight in the device's time zone; east of UTC that is the previous day in UTC, and every all-day event lands a day early. Convert to UTC midnight of the same calendar date.
* **Timed events:** use the event's `TZID` for `EVENT_TIMEZONE`. If the feed has no matching `VTIMEZONE`, the TZID is usually an Olson name Android knows; fall back to UTC only if it is not.
* **Recurring events** (`RRULE`): Android requires `DURATION` and forbids `DTEND` on them. Compute `DURATION` from the event's start and end.
* `RECURRENCE-ID` overrides need a separate row with `ORIGINAL_SYNC_ID` and `ORIGINAL_INSTANCE_TIME`. Few SchedJoules feeds use them; skipping them keeps the main series intact.

### Alarms

A `VALARM` in the feed becomes a row in `CalendarContract.Reminders` (`MINUTES` before, `METHOD_ALERT`). See [Alarms](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/alarms.md) for the defaults and the `al` parameter.

### Google Calendar and other devices

Events in a calendar under your own account type stay on the device. They show up in Google Calendar on that phone, but are not uploaded to the user's Google account, so they do not appear on the web or on other devices. That is how Android works for any calendar app that is not a Google account; tell your users rather than trying to work around it.

### Refreshing

* A periodic `WorkManager` job every few hours is enough. Android may delay it on low battery or in Doze; that is expected.
* Run a sync right after a subscription is added, so the user sees events at once.
* Keep the last `ETag` per feed and send it as `If-None-Match`.


<!-- source: details/ios.md -->

## iOS

On iOS there are two ways to get a SchedJoules calendar into the user's calendar. Pick one before you write code: they lead to different apps. Read the [Integration Guide](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/integration_guide.md) first.

| | Subscribed calendar (webcal) | Your app writes events (EventKit) |
|---|---|---|
| How | Open the feed URL with the `webcal://` scheme; iOS asks the user to confirm and then owns the calendar | Your app fetches the feed and writes events into a calendar it created with EventKit |
| Who refreshes | iOS, on its own schedule, without your app running | Your app, only when iOS lets it run |
| Effort for a v0.1 | Very small | Substantial |
| Freshness | Steady, independent of how often your app is opened | Depends on app opens, background refresh and pushes; can lag for users who rarely open your app |
| Personalisation (hide events, own alarms, combine sources) | Not possible | Possible |
| Removing the calendar | The user removes it in Settings or Calendar; your app cannot | Your app can |
| Calendar permission | Not needed | Needed (full access) |

For a v0.1, start with webcal: it works in an afternoon. Move to EventKit when you need personalisation.

### Webcal subscription

1. Build the feed URL as in the [Integration Guide](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/integration_guide.md#step-3-build-the-feed-url) (item `url` plus `&u=`).
2. Replace the scheme: `https://` becomes `webcal://`.
3. Open it with `UIApplication.shared.open(url)`. iOS shows its subscribe dialog.

Your app does not learn whether the user confirmed. To show "subscribed" in your UI, look for a calendar of type `.subscription` with the same title through EventKit afterwards, or simply keep your own list.

### EventKit

* Ask for calendar access (`requestFullAccessToEvents`) when the user subscribes to their first calendar, after explaining why; never at app start.
* Create one `EKCalendar` per subscription, on a writable source (iCloud or local), and keep its `calendarIdentifier` with the subscription.
* Map each feed event to an `EKEvent` and keep a map from the feed `UID` to the event's identifier. Apply changes by UID as the guide describes: add, update, delete only from complete feeds.
* All-day events: set `isAllDay` and use the date as given; do not shift it through a time zone.

**Refreshing.** iOS decides when your app may run in the background:
* Sync when the app starts and when it comes to the foreground.
* Schedule a `BGAppRefreshTask`. iOS runs it at its own discretion; do not count on a time.
* Silent pushes (`content-available`, priority 5) can wake your app, but Apple does not guarantee their delivery and asks for no more than two or three per hour.
* Nothing wakes your app when the user opens the Calendar app.

So freshness for EventKit users depends on how often they open your app. Plan for that: it is the main reason to start with webcal.


<!-- source: details/ui.md -->

## A Basic UI

A standalone v0.1 needs four screens. This is the structure the SchedJoules apps use on iOS and Android, reduced to what a first version needs. Build it with your platform's standard components (lists, tab or navigation bars, switches, sheets); nothing here needs a custom control. Read the [Integration Guide](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/integration_guide.md) first for the API side.

**Which screens to build:**

| Your app | Build |
|---|---|
| Already shows calendars or events (a calendar, agenda or planner app) | Browse and Calendar from this page, opened from your existing "add calendar" entry, as in [Embedding, pattern 3](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/embedding.md#pattern-3-a-source-among-sources). No My calendars or Settings screen: your own calendar list and settings do that job |
| Has no calendar views of its own, or is a standalone catalogue | All four screens below |
| Needs only one kind of content (public holidays, one sport) | No catalogue screens: [Embedding, pattern 1 or 2](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/embedding.md) |

The wireframes below show structure only: which elements, in which order. Draw them with your platform's own components and spacing.

| Screen | Shows | API |
|---|---|---|
| Browse | The catalogue, one page at a time, with search on top | `GET /pages`, `GET /pages/{id}`, `GET /pages/search` |
| Calendar | One calendar: its name, the next events, a subscribe control | The item from the page, and its feed |
| My calendars | What the user subscribed to | Your own storage |
| Settings | Country and language | `GET /countries`, `GET /languages` |

Put Browse and My calendars in a tab or navigation bar; Settings can be a third tab or sit behind an icon.

### Browse

```
+--------------------------------------+
| United States              (title)   |
| [ Search calendars               ]   |
|--------------------------------------|
| [icon] Holidays                  >   |   first section: no header
| [icon] Sports                    >   |
| POPULAR                   (header)   |
| [icon] Golden State Warriors  [on]   |   calendar row, subscribed
| [    ] Moon Phases            [  ]   |   icon null: empty space kept
|        Calendars by SchedJoules      |   attribution, end of the list
|--------------------------------------|
|  Browse  |  My calendars  |  Settings|
+--------------------------------------+
```

* Open on the user's home page: `GET /pages?locale={device language}&location={device country}`. Use the page's `name` as the screen title.
* Render each entry of `page_sections` as a list section with its `name` as the header. The first section can have an empty name: show it without a header.
* One row per item: the `icon` on the left, the `name` as the text.
  * `item_class: "page"`: a row with a chevron (or your platform's equivalent) that opens the child page as a new screen, with a back action to the parent.
  * `item_class: "calendar"`: a row that opens the Calendar screen. You may also put a subscribe switch on the row itself, so users can subscribe to several teams without leaving the list.
* `icon` can be `null` or missing. Reserve the space anyway and show a neutral placeholder, so the names stay aligned.
* Show which calendars the user already subscribed to, on the row (a filled switch, a check mark). Match by `item_id`.
* Search at the top of the home page. Send the query after the user typed 3 characters and paused briefly; show the results as one flat list, grouped by category if you like (see [Search](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/search.md)). Search names can end in a gender sign and a flag to tell teams apart: keep them in the result list, and use `original_name` everywhere else.

Optional for a later version: a "Top" tab with `GET /pages?top=20&location={country}` (see [Top, New, Next](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/top_new_next.md)), filter chips for the home page's sections.

### Calendar

What the user sees before and after subscribing to one calendar.

```
+--------------------------------------+
| <  Golden State Warriors             |
|--------------------------------------|
|          [ Subscribe ]               |   becomes "Subscribed"
|--------------------------------------|
| SAT 21 NOV                           |
|   19:30  Warriors - Lakers           |
| MON 23 NOV                           |
|   04:00  Celtics - Warriors          |
| ...                                  |   next 10 to 20 events
|        Calendars by SchedJoules      |   attribution
+--------------------------------------+
```

* Title: the item's `name` (`original_name` when it came from search).
* A subscribe control at the top: a switch or a button that turns into "Subscribed". Subscribing must give feedback at once; on Android, start the first sync immediately so events appear in the calendar app within seconds.
* Below it, the next events: fetch the [JSCalendar list](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/calendars.md#a-calendar-as-a-jscalendar-list) with `start_at_or_after` set to now and `results=20`, and list date, time and `title` of the entries, grouped by day. This lets users check that they picked the right team or region before they subscribe. An empty calendar gives `"entries": []`: show "No upcoming events". If you read the iCalendar feed here instead, never show its placeholder event (see [Integration Guide, step B2](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/integration_guide.md#step-b2-recognise-placeholder-events)).
* Tapping an event opens its detail screen. Fetch the event as [JSCalendar](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/calendars.md#one-event-as-jscalendar-rfc-8984), the recommended format: line-ups, results and holiday details as structured JSON. On any status other than `200` or `304`, show the feed's `DESCRIPTION`, `LOCATION` and `URL` instead.
* A calendar that needs input from the user asks for it here, before it can be subscribed:
  * weather: a city (with search) and units, see [Weather](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/weather.md)
  * pregnancy: the due date; countdown: a name and a date, see [Pregnancy and Countdown Calendars](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/user_input_calendars.md)

  Use the platform's date picker and a sheet or a separate screen. Never subscribe to the template URL with its `{placeholders}` still in it.

**With the test key** every calendar serves its real events, but only the next 5, so a Calendar screen previews at most 5 events and a synced calendar holds 5. That is expected and not a sync bug; your own key returns the whole calendar. To test the empty and placeholder states, load the files in [examples/feeds](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/tree/master/examples/feeds) instead of a live feed.

### My calendars

```
+--------------------------------------+
| My calendars                         |
|--------------------------------------|
| [icon] Golden State Warriors     (o) |   (o): colour in the system calendar
| [icon] Public Holidays           (o) |
| [icon] Moon Phases  Not syncing  (o) |   permission refused
|--------------------------------------|
|  Browse  |  My calendars  |  Settings|
+--------------------------------------+
```

* One row per subscription: icon, name, and on Android the colour of the calendar in the system calendar.
* Tapping a row opens the Calendar screen for that subscription.
* Unsubscribe from the Calendar screen or with a swipe on the row, after a confirmation. On Android, delete the local calendar and its events; with an iOS webcal subscription, tell the user to remove it under Calendar accounts in the iOS Settings app, because your app cannot.
* Empty state: one sentence and a button that opens Browse.

### Settings

```
+--------------------------------------+
| Settings                             |
|--------------------------------------|
| Country                United States |
| Language                     English |
| Contact support                    > |
+--------------------------------------+
```

* Country and language, both defaulting to the device. A change reloads the home page in Browse.
* Changing the language does not change existing subscriptions: their feeds stay in the language they were added in. Say so, or offer to re-add them.
* A link to your support channel.

### Attribution

Show **Calendars by SchedJoules** on Browse (every page and the search results) and on the Calendar screen: one line in your secondary text style, at the end of the list or under the title. My calendars and Settings do not need it. See [Attribution](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api#attribution) for the rules.

### Permissions and first run

* Do not ask for calendar access at app start. Ask when the user subscribes to the first calendar, after one line explaining why (Android: `READ_CALENDAR` and `WRITE_CALENDAR`; iOS with EventKit: full access; iOS with webcal: nothing).
* If the user refuses, keep the subscription in My calendars, show that it is not syncing, and link to the system settings.
* No onboarding is needed for a v0.1: the home page is the onboarding.

### States every screen needs

| State | Show |
|---|---|
| Loading | A progress indicator in the list area; keep the title and search visible |
| No network or `5xx` | A short message and a Retry button. Keep showing cached content if you have it |
| Empty page or search | "No calendars found" with the query |
| Calendar with no upcoming events | "No upcoming events"; the subscription itself is fine |

### Platform look

Use the native look of each platform instead of one shared design: system fonts, system colours and dark mode, the standard back behaviour, standard switches. Users recognise those, and they keep working with accessibility settings (larger text, screen readers) without extra effort. The iOS and Android SchedJoules apps share the same screens and grouping, but each looks like its own platform.

### A v0.1 UI checklist

Check each item in the running app, not only in code. Leave out the My calendars and Settings items when your app's own screens do that job (see the table at the top).

- [ ] Browse opens on the home page for the device's language and country, with the page `name` as title
- [ ] Sections show their `name` as header; a section with an empty name shows none
- [ ] Page rows open the child page with a working back action; calendar rows open the Calendar screen
- [ ] Rows with `icon: null` or no icon keep the names aligned
- [ ] Subscribed calendars are marked on their rows, matched by `item_id`, in Browse and in search results
- [ ] Search starts at 3 characters after a short pause; results use `original_name` once opened
- [ ] The Calendar screen title comes from the catalogue item, never from the feed's `X-WR-CALNAME`
- [ ] The Calendar screen lists the next events grouped by day, and shows "No upcoming events" for an empty list (or `empty.ics` when it reads the feed)
- [ ] No placeholder event is ever shown as an event (try every file in `examples/feeds/`)
- [ ] Tapping an event shows its JSCalendar document (try `examples/responses/event.jscalendar.json`), and the feed's `DESCRIPTION` when that request fails
- [ ] Subscribing gives feedback at once; on Android the first sync starts immediately
- [ ] Calendar access is asked at the first subscribe, not at app start; refusing it leaves the subscription visible as not syncing, with a link to the system settings
- [ ] Weather, pregnancy and countdown calendars ask for their input before subscribing
- [ ] Unsubscribing asks for confirmation and removes the events (Android) or explains the iOS Settings step (webcal)
- [ ] My calendars has an empty state with a button to Browse
- [ ] Changing country or language reloads Browse
- [ ] Loading, offline, `5xx`, empty search and empty calendar each show their state from the table above
- [ ] "Calendars by SchedJoules" shows on every Browse page, the search results and the Calendar screen
- [ ] Dark mode and the largest system text size both work on every screen


<!-- source: details/embedding.md -->

## Embedding the Catalogue in an Existing App

You do not need to show the whole catalogue. Most apps that already have users want SchedJoules content to appear as part of their own screens: a holidays switch in settings, a sports section next to their own content, an "Add calendar" option among the other sources. This page shows how to do that. For a separate catalogue screen instead, see [A Basic UI](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/ui.md). The feed rules in the [Integration Guide](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/integration_guide.md) apply either way.

Pick the pattern that fits where your users already are:

| Pattern | Looks like | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| [One switch](#pattern-1-one-switch) | "Show public holidays" in your settings | Smallest |
| [One branch](#pattern-2-one-branch) | A sports or TV section inside your app, showing one page of the catalogue | Small |
| [A source among sources](#pattern-3-a-source-among-sources) | "Add calendar > Holidays, sports and more" next to Google, iCloud or a URL | Medium |
| [Your own event view](#showing-the-events-in-your-own-views) | The events drawn in your app's own calendar or list, not through the system calendar | Depends on your app |

### Pattern 1: one switch

A single setting such as "Show public holidays for {country}". The user never sees the catalogue.

Find the country's national public holiday calendar with a filtered search:

```
GET /countries?locale={language}
  -> pick the user's country by iso_3166, take its country_id and name

GET /pages/search?q={country name}&country_id={country_id}&main_category_id=1&locale={language}
  -> take the calendar item with holiday_kind "public" and no region
```

For example `q=Germany&country_id=108&main_category_id=1` returns "Public Holidays" (`holiday_kind: "public"`, no `region`) together with the calendars of the 16 states, which carry a `region`. Use `holiday_kind: "observances"` for the variant that also includes observances (Mother's Day, Halloween), and the items with a `region` if you want to offer the user's state or province.

Then:
* Store the calendar's `item_id` and `url` once, and build the feed URL as usual (`url` + `&u=`).
* Do the lookup again when the user changes country, not on every start.
* Name the setting yourself ("Public holidays"); the item's `name` is generic ("Public Holidays") and does not mention the country.

The same lookup works for other single-calendar features: `holiday_kind: "school"` for school holidays, `main_category_id=2` with `sport_id` for a sport.

### Pattern 2: one branch

Show one page of the catalogue, and everything below it, inside your own screen: for example the sports of the user's country, a league, or the TV channels.

* Start from the country's home page (`page_id` from `GET /countries`, or `GET /pages?location={country}`) and pick the section you want by its items' `category_id` (see [Search](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/search.md) for the ids). Section names are translated and can change; category ids do not.
* Or start from a fixed page id, for a branch that is the same for all your users (a league, Formula 1). Agree the ids with us, so we know they are in use. If one answers `404`, fall back to the country's home page rather than showing an error. `GET /pages/{page_id}/info` returns the pages that list a page, which helps you check where it sits.
* Render the pages with your own list components, in your own style. The rules from [A Basic UI](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/ui.md#browse) still apply: icons can be `null`, show which calendars are subscribed, a page item opens the next page.
* Keep the user inside your app's navigation: a back action returns to your screen, not to a SchedJoules home page.

### Pattern 3: a source among sources

If your app already lets users add calendars (Google, iCloud, Exchange, a URL), add SchedJoules as one more source:

* The entry opens the user's home page (`GET /pages?locale=...&location=...`) with search on top, in a sheet or a pushed screen.
* Build the [Browse](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/ui.md#browse) and [Calendar](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/ui.md#calendar) screens from A Basic UI for this. Its My calendars and Settings screens are not needed: your calendar list and settings already do that job, and country and language become two of your settings.
* A subscribed calendar becomes a normal calendar in your app, with your app's controls: colour, visibility, notifications, remove. Do not build a separate "SchedJoules calendars" area.
* Show the calendar's name from the catalogue item (`original_name` from search), never from the feed's `X-WR-CALNAME`.
* SchedJoules calendars are read-only: hide editing on their events, and say so if the user tries.
* If your app already supports subscribing to a calendar by URL, you can reuse that path for the feed URL, as long as it follows the feed rules: body check, placeholder UIDs, sync by UID.

### Showing the events in your own views

Apps that draw their own calendar or agenda do not need the system calendar at all: fetch the feeds and store the events in your app's own local storage, then show them as a layer next to your own events.

* Store each event by its `UID`, linked to the subscription, so you can apply changes and remove the whole layer.
* All-day events (`DTSTART;VALUE=DATE`) are dates, not moments. Store and draw them as dates; converting them through a time zone moves them a day for some users.
* Timed events carry a `TZID`: convert to the user's time zone when drawing.
* Give each subscription its own colour and a visibility toggle, as you would for any other calendar.
* When the user opens an event, fetch it as [JSCalendar](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/calendars.md#one-event-as-jscalendar-rfc-8984), the recommended format for your own event view: the details users look for (scores, line-ups, results, holiday explanation) as structured JSON. Do not parse `DESCRIPTION` for them: its wording is not a contract. On any status other than `200` or `304`, show `DESCRIPTION` as plain text with line breaks.
* For a list screen that does not need the events stored (an agenda of one calendar, upcoming matches), read the [JSCalendar list](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/calendars.md#a-calendar-as-a-jscalendar-list) instead of the feed: titles and times only, a fraction of the size. Keep the layer in your calendar views synced from the feeds, as above.
* The data stays on the device: see [Data Usage and Restrictions](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api#data-usage-and-restrictions). If your app syncs calendars through your own servers, agree that with us first.

### Attribution

Wherever users choose SchedJoules content, show **Calendars by SchedJoules** (see [Attribution](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api#attribution)):

| Pattern | Where |
|---|---|
| One switch | The setting's supporting text: "Public holidays for Germany" with "Calendars by SchedJoules" below it |
| One branch | One line at the end of the branch's list, on every page of it |
| A source among sources | On the entry ("Holidays, sports and more", with "Calendars by SchedJoules" as its subtitle) and in the catalogue sheet it opens |
| Your own event view | On the detail view of a SchedJoules event, next to the calendar's name |

### What not to do

* Do not copy catalogue data into your own build or backend. Fetch pages when the user opens them; they change (new seasons, new teams, translations).
* Do not rewrite feed URLs or build them from ids. Always take the `url` from the item.
* Do not hide that a calendar can end: when a feed answers with a placeholder (see [Integration Guide, step B2](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/integration_guide.md#step-b2-recognise-placeholder-events)), show the state in your own UI.


<!-- source: details/pages.md -->

## Pages

Pages are the foundation of the API. They provide the structure for the views your users interact with; your application provides the UX and UI for each page.

Pages are localised: every translatable field is returned in the requested language.

`GET /pages/115673?locale=en` returns (shortened to one item per section):

```json
{
  "item_id": 115673,
  "name": "United States",
  "country": "United States",
  "country_id": 79,
  "icon": null,
  "page_sections": [
    {
      "name": "Holidays",
      "id": 2,
      "items": [
        {
          "item_class": "calendar",
          "item": {
            "item_id": 50084,
            "name": "Public Holidays",
            "url": "https://holidays.schedjoules.com/calendars/766e8a162f82?l=en",
            "category": "Holidays",
            "category_id": 1,
            "country": "United States",
            "country_id": 79,
            "holiday_kind": "public",
            "icon": "https://cdn-images.schedjoules.com/assets/9783d4f3.png"
          }
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "Sports",
      "id": 28,
      "items": [
        {
          "item_class": "page",
          "item": {
            "item_id": 29230902,
            "name": "NBA",
            "url": "https://api.schedjoules.com/pages/29230902?locale=en",
            "category": "Sports",
            "category_id": 2,
            "country": "United States",
            "country_id": 79,
            "sport": "Basketball",
            "sport_id": 2,
            "gender": "Men",
            "gender_id": 1,
            "icon": "https://cdn-images.schedjoules.com/assets/basketball.png"
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

An optional field without a value is usually left out rather than sent as `null`; `icon` is the exception and can be `null`.

### Page

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `item_id` | integer | Always. Unique per page |
| `name` | string | Always |
| `page_sections` | array | Always. One or more sections |
| `icon` | string (URL) or null | |
| `description` | string | |
| `url` | string (URL) | Only on a page that has no sections of its own |
| `app_subscription_identifier` | string | Only for API keys on a subscription pricing model. The product identifier to offer this user. It can differ per user: it is chosen from the `u` parameter (or the `x-user-id` header) |

A page also carries the same tag fields as an item (`category`, `country`, `sport` and so on, see below) when they apply.

### Page Section

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | Always. An empty string for the first, unnamed section |
| `id` | integer | Not on the first, unnamed section |
| `items` | array | The section's items |

### Item

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `item_class` | string | `page` or `calendar` |
| `item` | object | The page item or calendar item |

### Page item and calendar item

Both have the same fields. The difference is the `url`: a page item's `url` is the API URL of the child page, a calendar item's `url` is the calendar feed.

| Field | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `item_id` | integer | Always |
| `name` | string | Always |
| `url` | string (URL) | Always |
| `icon` | string (URL) or null | |
| `category`, `category_id` | string, integer | Main category, see [Search](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/search.md) for the ids |
| `country`, `country_id` | string, integer | The country the item belongs to, see [Countries](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/countries.md) |
| `region`, `region_id` | string, integer | Regional holiday calendars only |
| `sport`, `sport_id` | string, integer | Sports only |
| `gender`, `gender_id` | string, integer | Sports only: 1 Men, 2 Women, 3 Unspecified, 4 Mixed |
| `holiday_kind` | string | Holiday calendars only, for example `public` |

`region` is set on regional holiday calendars only: the state, province or other region the calendar covers, in the requested locale (falling back to English). `country` is the country it belongs to; a national calendar has no `region`. Outside its parent page a regional calendar is named like its national one ("Public Holidays and Observances"), so show `region` with it, for example as a subtitle: "California, United States".

Before presenting a calendar item's `url` to your users, append the unique anonymous user identifier: `&u={unique_anonymous_user_identifier}` (see the [README](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api#unique-anonymous-user-identifier)).

A calendar `url` can be a template that your app must fill in first, such as the weather calendar's `{location}`. See [Weather](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/weather.md) and [Pregnancy and Countdown Calendars](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/user_input_calendars.md).


<!-- source: details/calendars.md -->

## Calendars

The `url` of a calendar item is the calendar feed. Remember to append `&u={unique_anonymous_user_identifier}` to every calendar URL (see the [README](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api#unique-anonymous-user-identifier)).

### Formats

| Format | Status | URL |
|---|---|---|
| **JSCalendar** ([RFC 8984](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8984)) | **Recommended.** Our newest format and the default choice for new integrations, for every event your app reads and shows itself | List: `.../calendars/766e8a162f82.jscalendar?...`<br>One event: `...&event={event part}` |
| **iCalendar** ([RFC 5545](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5545)) | **Most widely used.** What the feed URL returns. Every major operating system and calendar client can subscribe to it | `.../calendars/766e8a162f82` |
| jCal ([RFC 7265](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7265)) | Works, not recommended | `.../calendars/766e8a162f82.json` |
| xCal ([RFC 6321](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6321)) | Works, not recommended | `.../calendars/766e8a162f82.xml` |

**JSCalendar** is plain JSON with structured data: a match's line-ups, a race classification, a holiday's background, a company event's details. It is an IETF standard, built as the JSON successor to iCalendar, and the API is developing it further: new data arrives in JSCalendar first. See [A Calendar as a JSCalendar List](#a-calendar-as-a-jscalendar-list), [One Event as JSCalendar](#one-event-as-jscalendar-rfc-8984) and [Why JSCalendar](#why-jscalendar).

**iCalendar** is the format we suggest for subscribing users and syncing events into the device calendar. JSCalendar can be used for subscribing and syncing too, but most calendar clients read only iCalendar, so the sync track of the [Integration Guide](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/integration_guide.md#track-b-sync-into-a-calendar) is written for iCalendar.

**jCal and xCal** are iCalendar mapped one to one into JSON and XML. They are still served and follow their RFCs, but they carry no more than the iCalendar feed: no structured data, and no alarms. Do not start a new integration on them. For JSON, use JSCalendar; for subscribing and syncing, use iCalendar.

### Which Format to Use

The recommended pattern is a short list first, details per event:

1. **Subscribe and sync with iCalendar.** Calendar apps, webcal subscriptions and the device calendar read the feed.
2. **List events in your own screens from the [JSCalendar list](#a-calendar-as-a-jscalendar-list)**: the whole calendar with only what a list needs (title, time, duration, status, location), a fraction of the size of the iCalendar feed.
3. **Fetch the full JSCalendar `Event` when the user opens one**: the description and the structured data. See [One Event as JSCalendar](#one-event-as-jscalendar-rfc-8984).

| You want to | Use |
|---|---|
| Subscribe a user, or sync the events into the device calendar | iCalendar |
| Show a list of a calendar's events in your app: an agenda, upcoming matches | JSCalendar list |
| Show an event in detail: a match with its line-ups, a race classification, a holiday's background | JSCalendar `Event`, one per request |

JSCalendar can be used for subscribing and syncing too, but most calendar clients read only iCalendar. That is why we suggest the iCalendar feed for syncing.

### One Event as JSCalendar (RFC 8984)

```
GET /calendars/766e8a162f82.jscalendar?{the feed's own parameters}&event={event part}
Accept: application/jscalendar+json
```

Take the calendar item's `url` exactly as you use it for the feed, including `&u=`, add `.jscalendar` to the path and append `&event=`. The request passes the same access checks and returns events from the same window as the feed.

The **event part** comes from the event's `UID` in the feed. A UID has the form `{page id}_{language id}_{event part}@schedjoules.com`: drop the domain and the first two fields. The event part can itself contain underscores.

* UID `49733_1_28_1__20261205@schedjoules.com` → `event=28_1__20261205`
* UID `36254089_1_5781805@schedjoules.com` → `event=5781805`

Calendars whose UIDs do not start with the page id, such as weather, have no event documents.

#### Responses

| Status | Body | When |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | JSCalendar `Event`, `application/jscalendar+json` | The event is in the feed this URL serves |
| 304 | none | `If-None-Match` matches. The ETag is per event |
| 403 | `{"error":"no_access"}` or `{"error":"expired_subscription"}` | Where the feed would serve a placeholder event |
| 404 | `{"error":"event_not_found"}` | The event is not in this feed: outside the window, removed, or unknown |
| 404 | `{"error":"expired_calendar"}` | The calendar is retired |

On any status other than 200 or 304, show what you already have from the feed (title, time, `DESCRIPTION`).

Unlike the feed, access problems come back as HTTP errors, not as a `200` with a placeholder event.

#### The Document

Standard JSCalendar properties are written by the same code that writes the iCalendar feed, so for the same `UID` they always agree with it:

| iCalendar | JSCalendar |
|---|---|
| `UID` | `uid` |
| `SUMMARY` | `title` |
| `DTSTART`, `DTEND` with a time (UTC) | `start` (local date-time), `timeZone: "Etc/UTC"`, `duration` |
| `DTSTART`, `DTEND` as dates (all-day) | `start` at `T00:00:00`, `showWithoutTime: true`, `duration` in days, no `timeZone` |
| `LOCATION`, `GEO` | `locations."1"` with `name` and `coordinates` (`geo:lat,lon`) |
| `URL` | `links."1"` with `href`, `rel: "alternate"` |
| `LAST-MODIFIED` | `updated` |
| `STATUS` | `status`: `confirmed`, `tentative` or `cancelled` |
| `DESCRIPTION` | `description`, with real line breaks |

Empty properties are left out.

Structured data is in vendor properties, named under our domain as RFC 8984 section 3.3 prescribes:

| Property | Calendars | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `schedjoules.com:version` | all | `1`. Within a version, changes are additive only |
| `schedjoules.com:competition` | sports, except motorsport and cycling | the competition the match belongs to, such as `Eredivisie`, as a string. Also on [list](#a-calendar-as-a-jscalendar-list) entries, to label rows |
| `schedjoules.com:match` | football | `status`, `competition`, score, `home` and `away` with team, formation, starters and bench, and a timeline of goals, cards and substitutions |
| `schedjoules.com:raceResults` | motorsport, cycling | rows of `position`, `name`, `points`, `time`, `status` (`DNF`, `DNS`, `DSQ`, ...) |
| `schedjoules.com:holiday` | national and regional holidays | `observedIn` (list), `estimated` (bool), `text` |
| `schedjoules.com:finance` | company calendars | `company`, `bank`, `extraInfo`, `extraInfoUrl`, `speaker`, `webcast`, `irContact` (`name`, `email`, `phone`) |

Other calendars (TV, school holidays, moon phases, week numbers, name days and more) have the standard properties only: show their `description`. More vendor properties will be added over time. Ignore the ones you do not know, as RFC 8984 requires, and fall back to `description` for any event you have no layout for.

Football:

```json
{
  "@type": "Event",
  "uid": "36254089_1_5781805@schedjoules.com",
  "updated": "2026-11-20T10:00:00Z",
  "title": "NEC Nijmegen - PSV Eindhoven",
  "start": "2026-11-21T19:00:00",
  "timeZone": "Etc/UTC",
  "duration": "PT1H45M",
  "status": "confirmed",
  "description": "Tournament: Eredivisie\n\n...",
  "locations": { "1": { "@type": "Location", "name": "Goffertstadion, Nijmegen", "coordinates": "geo:51.8231,5.83813" } },
  "links": { "1": { "@type": "Link", "href": "https://www.schedjoules.com/calendar/36254089?event=5781805&c=event", "rel": "alternate" } },
  "schedjoules.com:version": 1,
  "schedjoules.com:competition": "Eredivisie",
  "schedjoules.com:match": { "id": 5781805, "status": "scheduled", "competition": "Eredivisie", "home": { "team": "NEC Nijmegen", "formation": "3-4-3", "starters": [], "bench": [] }, "away": { "team": "PSV Eindhoven", "starters": [], "bench": [] }, "events": [] }
}
```

Holiday:

```json
{
  "@type": "Event",
  "uid": "49733_1_28_1__20261205@schedjoules.com",
  "title": "Saint Nicholas",
  "start": "2026-12-05T00:00:00",
  "showWithoutTime": true,
  "duration": "P1D",
  "status": "confirmed",
  "description": "Saint Nicholas Day, celebrated on December 6th, ...",
  "locations": { "1": { "@type": "Location", "name": "Netherlands" } },
  "schedjoules.com:version": 1,
  "schedjoules.com:holiday": { "estimated": false, "text": "Saint Nicholas Day, celebrated on December 6th, ..." }
}
```

### A Calendar as a JSCalendar List

Leave out `event` and the same request returns the whole calendar as a JSCalendar `Group` ([RFC 8984 section 5.3](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8984#section-5.3)), for an event list in your app:

```
GET /calendars/766e8a162f82.jscalendar?{the feed's own parameters}
Accept: application/jscalendar+json
```

```json
{
  "@type": "Group",
  "uid": "36254089_1@schedjoules.com",
  "title": "Eredivisie (Netherlands)",
  "entries": [
    {
      "@type": "Event",
      "uid": "36254089_1_5781805@schedjoules.com",
      "updated": "2026-11-20T10:00:00Z",
      "title": "NEC Nijmegen - PSV Eindhoven",
      "start": "2026-11-21T19:00:00",
      "timeZone": "Etc/UTC",
      "duration": "PT1H45M",
      "status": "confirmed",
      "locations": { "1": { "@type": "Location", "name": "Goffertstadion, Nijmegen", "coordinates": "geo:51.8231,5.83813" } },
      "schedjoules.com:competition": "Eredivisie"
    }
  ],
  "schedjoules.com:version": 1
}
```

* Each entry has the list properties only: `uid`, `updated`, `title`, `start`, `timeZone` or `showWithoutTime`, `duration`, `status`, `locations` and, for a match, `schedjoules.com:competition`. They have the same values as in the [event's own document](#the-document). For the description, links and structured data, fetch that document with the entry's event part when the user opens it.
* The entries are the events of the iCalendar feed, in the same order. [`start_at_or_after`, `start_before`](#date-range), [`results`](#number-of-events) and [`events_updated_since`](#incremental-updates) work as they do for the feed. A called-off match in an `events_updated_since` answer has `status: "cancelled"`.
* A calendar without events gives `"entries": []`, never a placeholder event.
* Errors, `ETag` and `304` work as for one event. The list has an `ETag` of its own.
* It is much smaller than the feed. Measured on 2026-11-21: Eredivisie (500 events) 165 KB against 590 KB for the iCalendar feed, 9 KB against 70 KB gzipped.

The list alone is not enough to sync from: it has no descriptions, so events would arrive without their details. Syncing from JSCalendar takes the list plus each event's own document. To fill the device calendar, use the iCalendar feed: most calendar clients read only iCalendar.

#### Why JSCalendar

* **No parsing of description text.** In iCalendar, a match's line-ups, a race classification or a holiday's background only exist as free text in `DESCRIPTION`, and the wording of that text is not a contract: it can change at any time. The vendor properties are a contract, versioned and changed additively only.
* **Plain JSON.** No iCalendar parser, line folding, escaping or `VTIMEZONE` handling for a screen that shows one event. Any JSON library reads it.
* **Agrees with the user's calendar.** The standard properties come from the same code as the feed, so the detail screen never shows a different time or title than the event the user synced.
* **A published standard, not a SchedJoules format.** JSCalendar is an IETF standard (RFC 8984), designed as a JSON alternative to iCalendar and the event format of JMAP for Calendars. jCal maps iCalendar one to one, so its `DESCRIPTION` is still text; JSCalendar is built to carry structured data.
* **Safe to build on.** Unknown vendor properties are ignored and `description` is always there, so a new kind of data or a new field never breaks your app.
* **Small and cacheable.** One event per request, with a per-event `ETag` for `If-None-Match`, instead of downloading the whole feed to show one event. For a list screen, the [JSCalendar list](#a-calendar-as-a-jscalendar-list) is a fraction of the feed's size.
* **Clear errors.** Access problems are HTTP statuses, so there are no placeholder events to recognise.

### Date Range

By default, the date range of events returned depends on your agreement with SchedJoules. You can narrow it:

```
GET /calendars/766e8a162f82?start_at_or_after={datetime}&start_before={datetime}

Optional GET parameters
- start_at_or_after     datetime    ISO 8601 (e.g. 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z). Only events
                                    starting at or after this moment are returned.
- start_before          datetime    ISO 8601. Only events starting before this moment
                                    are returned.
```

`start_before` can only shorten the window: a value later than the end of the window your agreement gives has no effect. A value that cannot be parsed is ignored. The weather calendar ignores both parameters.

### Number of Events

By default, every event in the date range is returned. To limit the response to the first N events:

```
GET /calendars/766e8a162f82?results={nr_of_events}

Optional GET parameters
- results               integer     Maximum number of events to return.
```

### Incremental Updates

To fetch only the events that changed since a given moment:

```
GET /calendars/766e8a162f82?events_updated_since={timestamp}

Optional GET parameters
- events_updated_since  Returns only events updated after this moment.
```

The format currently depends on the calendar type:
* **National holiday calendars:** Unix time in seconds, for example `1767225600`.
* **Regional holiday calendars and most sport calendars:** an ISO 8601 datetime, for example `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z`.
* **All other calendars:** the parameter is ignored, and you get the full calendar.

When you ask a sport calendar for updates, events that were called off are included, so you can remove them on your side.

### Hiding Sport Event Results
Some users prefer not to see results in a sport event's title, for example because they will watch the match later. Use `show_result=false` to leave results out:

```
GET /calendars/d2b1e319a12a?show_result=false

Optional GET parameters
- show_result           Only the value 'false' has an effect. Results are shown by default.
```

### Alarms
See [Alarms](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/alarms.md).

### Calendars Filled In by the User
The weather, pregnancy and countdown calendars have a URL template that your app fills in with what the user enters (a location, a due date, or a name and a date). See [Weather](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/weather.md) and [Pregnancy and Countdown Calendars](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/user_input_calendars.md).


<!-- source: details/user_input_calendars.md -->

## Calendars Filled In by the User

Most calendar URLs in a pages response can be subscribed to as they are. A few calendars are built from something the user enters in your app before subscribing, the way the [weather calendar](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/weather.md) needs a location. Their URL is a template with placeholders in curly braces, and your app replaces each placeholder with the user's input.

There are two such calendars:

| Calendar | Placeholders | What it shows |
|---|---|---|
| Pregnancy | `{due_date}` | One event per week of pregnancy, counted back from the due date, plus the due date itself |
| Countdown | `{countdown_name}`, `{countdown_date}`, `{countdown_yearly}` | One all-day event per day up to a date the user picks, for example "12 days to Holiday" |

SchedJoules stores none of this input. Everything the calendar needs is in the URL, and every request computes the events from it. Keep the filled URL as the subscription: changing the input means subscribing to a new URL (or replacing the old one).

### Availability: announce the input step

These pages only appear in API responses for apps that can fill the template. An app announces that with the `features` parameter on its API requests:

```
GET /pages/115673?locale=en&location=us&features=due_date,countdown

Optional GET parameters
- features      comma separated list of input steps the app supports
                due_date    shows the pregnancy calendar
                countdown   shows the countdown calendar
```

The parameter applies to every request that returns pages: `/pages`, `/pages/{page_id}`, search, and the top, new and next lists. A request without it never sees these pages, so an app that cannot fill the template does not show its users a calendar they cannot use.

At the moment these pages are served to the SchedJoules apps only, whatever the `features` parameter says. Contact support@schedjoules.com if you would like to offer them in your app.

### Recognising a template

Check the calendar item's `url` for a placeholder before you present a subscribe action. A URL that still contains `{` and `}` (or their encoded form `%7B` and `%7D`) must never be subscribed to as it is: an unfilled template serves an empty calendar.

Do not add these calendars through a one-tap path that skips the input step, such as a suggestion or onboarding list.

### Pregnancy

The calendar item's URL looks like this:

```
https://xxx.schedjoules.com/calendars/xxxxxxxxxxxx?l=en&due={due_date}&x=xxx
```

Replace `{due_date}` with the due date as `YYYY-MM-DD`, then append `&u={unique_anonymous_user_identifier}` as for any other calendar.

| Parameter | Format | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `due` | `YYYY-MM-DD` | Accepted from 365 days in the past up to 294 days (42 weeks) ahead |

The calendar contains:
* One all-day event per week, from week 4 to week 42. Weeks are completed weeks as midwives count them: week 12 runs from 12+0 to 12+6, and week 40 starts on the due date.
* One all-day event on the due date itself.

Each event has a title ("Week 12: ...") and a description of the baby's development in that week, written from the NHS week-by-week guide and translated into every API language. The descriptions are general information, not medical advice, and each ends with a disclaimer saying so.

The due date is health data. Do not log the filled URL or send it to analytics.

### Countdown

The calendar item's URL looks like this:

```
https://xxx.schedjoules.com/calendars/xxxxxxxxxxxx?l=en&countdown_name={countdown_name}&countdown_date={countdown_date}&countdown_yearly={countdown_yearly}&x=xxx
```

Fill in the placeholders, append `countdown_repeat` (below) and `&u={unique_anonymous_user_identifier}`.

| Parameter | Format | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `countdown_name` | text, URL-encoded | What the user counts down to. Whitespace is collapsed and the name is cut at 60 characters |
| `countdown_date` | `YYYY-MM-DD` | The day counted down to. Up to 10 years ahead |
| `countdown_repeat` | `none`, `yearly`, `monthly`, `weekly` | How the countdown repeats. Not in the template yet: append it. Any other value means `none` |
| `countdown_yearly` | `1` or `0` | The older form of `countdown_repeat`: `1` means yearly. Used only when `countdown_repeat` is missing. Fill it as well, so the URL works the same either way |

The calendar is named after the countdown, so a user with several countdowns can tell them apart in their calendar app. Each event is an all-day event:

* Every day before the date: "12 days to Holiday"
* On the date itself: "Holiday is today"

Which days get an event depends on the repeat:

| Repeat | Events | After the date |
|---|---|---|
| `none` | The 365 days before the date, and the date | Nothing. A date more than 365 days in the past gives an empty calendar |
| `yearly` | The 365 days before the next anniversary, and the anniversary | Rolls on to next year's anniversary |
| `monthly` | From the day after the previous occurrence up to the next one | Rolls on to the next month. A 31st falls on the last day of a shorter month |
| `weekly` | The 6 days before the next occurrence of that weekday, and the day itself | Rolls on to the next week |

For a repeating countdown the date is the first occurrence and may lie in the past, so a birthday can be entered with the year of birth.

The texts are available in en, ar, da, de, es, fi, fr, it, ja, ko, nl, no, pl, pt, ru, sv, tr and zh. Other languages get English.

The name is text the user typed. Do not log the filled URL or send it to analytics.

### Date Range

Both calendars follow the same [date range](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/calendars.md#date-range) rules as every other calendar, and the `start_at_or_after`, `start_before` and `results` parameters work as usual.

### Unusable Input

A missing, malformed or out-of-range value never causes an error. The request succeeds with an empty calendar. Validate the input in your app before subscribing, using the ranges above, so the user is not left with a calendar that never shows anything.


<!-- source: details/weather.md -->

## Weather

### Calendar Requests

The weather calendar is a forecast for one location, 16 days ahead, with one all-day event per day. Its `url` in a pages response is a template your app fills in:

```
GET /calendars/weather/calendar.ics?l={locale}&loc={location}&d={temp}&p={rain}&w={wind}&t={time}

Required GET parameters
- loc   location        location_id from GET /cities/search or GET /cities/cities_within_bounds (below)

Optional GET parameters
- l     locale          ISO 639-1 language code (default: 'en')
- d     temperature     c, f (default: 'c')
- w     wind speed      kmh, kts, ms, mph (default: 'kmh')
- t     time format     12, 24 (default: 24)
- p     precipitation   mm, in. Accepted, but has no effect: the calendar shows no precipitation
- h     hourly          1 = one detail line per hour for the first 96 hours instead of one per 3 hours
```

Each day's event contains:
* in the title: the day's minimum and maximum temperature and a short description of the weather;
* in the description: a line every 3 hours (or every hour with `h=1`) with temperature, wind speed and conditions, followed by the day's temperature, humidity and wind range.

### Weather Settings

The units to offer, with localised names and the default for a country:

```
GET /cities/weather_settings?locale={locale}&location={ISO 3166 code}

Optional GET parameters
- locale        (default: 'en')
- location      country whose defaults to return. Only 'us' and 'gb' have their own defaults
```

`GET /cities/weather_settings?locale=en&location=us` returns:

```json
{
  "temp": {"title": "Temperature", "options": {"c": "ºC", "f": "ºF"}, "default": "f"},
  "rain": {"title": "Precipitation", "options": {"mm": "mm", "in": "po"}, "default": "in"},
  "wind": {"title": "Wind Speed", "options": {"kmh": "km/h", "kts": "Knots", "ms": "m/s", "mph": "mph"}, "default": "mph"},
  "time": {"title": "Time format", "options": {"12": "12-hour", "24": "24-hour"}, "default": "12"}
}
```

### Searching Locations by City Name

```
GET /cities/search?q={query}

Required GET parameters
- q         search query, at least 2 characters

Optional GET parameters
- locale    returns city names in this language where available
```

Every word of the query must match the start of a word in the city's name or one of its local names. At most 10 results, ordered by exact name match first, then names that start with the query, then popularity. A query shorter than 2 characters returns an empty array `[]`.

`GET /cities/search?q=Amsterdam` returns (shortened):

```json
{
  "cities": [
    {"country": "nl", "latitude": 52.37, "longitude": 4.9, "name": "Amsterdam", "location_id": 102759794},
    {"country": "ca", "latitude": 51.75, "longitude": -102.47, "name": "Amsterdam", "location_id": 105884628}
  ]
}
```

Use the `location_id` as the `loc` parameter of the calendar URL. `country` is a lowercase ISO 3166 code.

### Locations on a Map

To show weather locations on a map of the area the user is looking at:

```
GET /cities/cities_within_bounds?ne={lat},{lng}&sw={lat},{lng}

Required GET parameters
- ne    north-east corner of the visible map, latitude first
- sw    south-west corner of the visible map, latitude first
```

The API takes the 100 most popular locations in the area and groups nearby ones, so you get at most 30 markers. A north-east longitude smaller than the south-west one is read as an area that crosses the 180° meridian.

`GET /cities/cities_within_bounds?ne=52.5,5.1&sw=52.2,4.7` returns (shortened):

```json
[
  {"la": 52.37, "lo": 4.9, "fo": 102759794, "ty": "i", "to": "Amsterdam"},
  {"la": 52.3, "lo": 4.86, "fo": 102759798, "ty": "i", "to": "Amstelveen"}
]
```

| Field | |
|---|---|
| `la`, `lo` | Latitude and longitude |
| `fo` | The `location_id` |
| `to` | Location name |
| `ty` | `i` for a single location, `c` for a cluster of several. A cluster carries the name and id of one of its locations; zoom in to split it |


<!-- source: details/alarms.md -->

## Alarms

Events in the iCalendar feed carry a default alarm that depends on the type of calendar:

| Calendar | Default alarm |
|---|---|
| Sports | 30 minutes before |
| TV | 30 minutes before |
| Moon phases, name days, week numbers, day numbers | 30 minutes before |
| Finance | 720 minutes (12 hours) before |
| Public holidays | none |
| School holidays | 720 minutes before for most countries, 30 minutes before in the UK |
| Weather, pregnancy, countdown | none |

You can override the default, or let your users do so, with the `al` parameter on the calendar URL:

| Value | Effect |
|---|---|
| `al=48` | Alarm 48 minutes before the start of each event |
| `al=-15` | Alarm 15 minutes after the start |
| `al=0` | Alarm at the start. Any value that is not a number has the same effect |
| `al=none` | No alarms |

`al` also adds alarms to calendars that have none by default. It only applies to the iCalendar format: jCal and xCal responses contain no alarms.


<!-- source: details/search.md -->

## Search

Free-text search over calendars and pages:

```
GET /pages/search?q={query}

e.g. /pages/search?q=Warriors

Required GET parameters
- q                     string   at least 3 characters. A shorter query returns no items

Optional GET parameters
- locale                string   (default: 'en')
- nr_results            integer  number of results (default and maximum: 50)
- country_id            integer  filter by country, see Countries
- main_category_id      integer  filter by main category
- sport_id              integer  filter by sport
- gender_id             integer  filter by gender
```

Every filter takes one id or a comma-separated list, e.g. `main_category_id=1,2`. An unknown id returns no items, not an error.

`main_category_id` values:

| ID | Category |
|---|---|
| 1 | Holidays |
| 2 | Sports |
| 3 | Weather |
| 4 | Finance |
| 5 | Miscellaneous |
| 6 | TV |

`gender_id` values: 1 Men, 2 Women, 3 Unspecified, 4 Mixed.

See [Countries](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/countries.md) for `country_id`. To open a page whose id you already know, use `GET /pages/{page_id}`; there is no separate lookup endpoint.

### Response

The response has the [pages](https://github.com/schedjoules/calendar-store-api/blob/master/details/pages.md) structure, with `item_id` set to `null` and the query as `name`. Results are grouped into one section per main category. Search items carry one extra field, `original_name`: `name` may include a gender sign and a flag to tell similar teams apart, `original_name` does not.

`GET /pages/search?q=Warriors&nr_results=1` returns:

```json
{
  "item_id": null,
  "name": "Warriors",
  "page_sections": [
    {
      "name": "Sports",
      "items": [
        {
          "item_class": "calendar",
          "item": {
            "item_id": 29139585,
            "name": "Golden State Warriors ♂ 🇺🇸",
            "original_name": "Golden State Warriors",
            "url": "https://holidays.schedjoules.com/calendars/766e8a162f82?l=en",
            "category": "Sports",
            "category_id": 2,
```
